impl.api_review:
RC-36 for T1, at the tip b7ac3ec.
PUBLIC tui4s, added: `Tui.run(ui: (Unit < Sync) => UI < (Async & Scope))(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Abort[TuiError])` and `Tui.run(options: TuiOptions)(ui: (Unit < Sync) => UI < (Async & Scope))(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Abort[TuiError])` (the shape of Headless.start: the UI gets the quit value, D-15; Tui.quit of C3 is the second way; no public Tui.start, no TuiHandle). `enum TuiError(message: String, cause: Throwable | Null) extends Exception(message, cause)` (Kyo-free; a KyoApp main shows it): `NotATerminal(error: Throwable)` "stdin/stdout is not a terminal"; `NativeAccessDenied(error: Throwable)` "start the JVM with --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED"; `NativeLoadFailed(error: Throwable)` "the native terminal library (crossterm) could not be loaded: <cause>" (new, bot fix Crossterm.scala:103); `TerminalIO(error: Throwable)` "terminal I/O failed". PR 5 cases AppFailed and SourceFailed dropped (their features are gone: a failure of the UI comes out as it is after the restore; handler failures are logged, C3). No CanEqual on TuiError (an exception, matched by case). `TuiOptions` fields added at the end with Scaladoc, defaults: `pollInterval: java.time.Duration = Duration.ofMillis(25)` (negative counts as zero), `inboxCapacity: Int = 1024` (below 1 counts as 1; a full inbox makes the input thread and the watchers wait, nothing dropped), `captureOutput: Boolean = true` (opt-out), `logFile: Option[java.nio.file.Path] = None` (None: the last 200 lines in memory, printed to stderr after the restore); `derives CanEqual` stays; Kyo-free. No fps, mouse, focusEvents, viewport, theme, trace. Unchanged: Tui.quit, FrameStats, FrameCause. Package Scaladoc updated.
PUBLIC tui4s.spi: no change. PR 5's public spi.InputPort is not public any more: with D-21 a its element is the crossterm Event (a jatatui type), so it is private[tui4s] in tui4s.internal.
PUBLIC tui4s.testkit: no signature change; Headless.start uses options.inboxCapacity for its inbox (was 4096). RecordingControl and ScriptedInput are test doubles in the TEST sources (private[tui4s]).
Kyo types in new public signatures: UI, <, Sync, Async, Scope, Abort, Frame (as Headless.start). No jatatui, crossterm or Kyo-internal type: PublicApiTest gets a third leaf (TASTy: no public signature of tui4s, tui4s.spi, tui4s.testkit names jatatui.* or tui.crossterm.*), red with a public Headless.leakedBackend: TestBackend, green at the tip.
THE SEAL stays: every top-level definition of tui4s.internal is private[tui4s], including the new TerminalIO, Hooks, Crossterm, NativeCrossterm, Tty, CrosstermInput, InputPort, TerminalControl, Session, InputThread, EventMapping, OutputCapture, LogSink, TuiLog (PublicApiTest leaf 1); no public signature names an internal type (leaf 2).

impl.pr_body:
After the merge, a kyo-ui app runs in a real terminal: `tui4s.Tui.run(options)(ui)` and `tui4s.Tui.run(ui)` put the terminal in raw mode, enter the alternate screen, start an input thread that maps the crossterm events to kyo-ui keys, pastes and resizes, run the C2/C3 runner on a crossterm backend, and restore the terminal in every way that a run ends (a quit, a failure, an interrupt, the JVM shutdown hook). `ui` gets the quit value (as in `Headless.start`); `Tui.quit` and Ctrl-C end the run too. A run that cannot start fails with a Kyo-free `tui4s.TuiError` before the terminal changes. The Counter example runs from a start script (`sbt examples/launchers`, then `examples/target/bin/counter`), and a PTY kit checks it in a pseudo-terminal, locally and in the new CI job `terminal`. The three bot findings of the old PRs 4 and 5 are fixed, each in its own commit with a regression test and a negative control. Base: PR #13 (C3, `feat/kyoui-03-input`, f29b9ff).

The carry commit is byte-identical to PR 5 (666a8e3) and the prototype (1d100ed), and the format commit only removes the 39 old marks. One major finding (R1-1): the headless kit (C3 code) sends an upper-case letter with no modifiers. Through crossterm 0.29 (whose legacy parser marks every upper-case char SHIFT) and EventMapping, the real terminal gives the same letter `shift = true`. A handler that matches `Modifiers.none` can pass on Headless and never fire for capitals in the terminal. The fix is small: the kit gives shift to an upper-case character, plus a parity test. Confirm first with the implementer's Probe.java, because I did not run anything.

findings.claim: A `pollInterval` of zero turns the input thread into a busy loop: `pollMillis` floors at 0, `NativeCrossterm.poll(0)` gives crossterm a zero `Duration` that returns at once, and the outer `while running do if port.poll(pollMillis)` spins at 100 percent of one CPU. The Scaladoc says 'A negative interval counts as zero', so zero reads as an allowed value.
findings.evidence: Session.scala:186-187 `opts.pollInterval.toMillis.max(0L)...`; Crossterm.scala:287-288 `val ms = timeoutMillis.max(0); native.poll(CDuration(ms / 1000L, (ms % 1000) * 1_000_000))`; InputThread.run has no sleep when poll returns false. `ScriptedInput.poll` (test double) also returns at once for 0 (`queue.poll(0, ms)`). No test sets `pollInterval = Duration.ZERO`.

findings.claim: After a normal quit, the terminal restore waits for the UI's own Scope to close: `Scope.run(runner.scoped(ui(quit).map(runner.run)))` sits inside the `acquireReleaseWith` use, and Kyo's `Fiber.init` release interrupts each UI fiber AND awaits its result (`fiber.interrupt.andThen(Async.useResult(promise)(...))`, Kyo Fiber.scala:142-150; `Scope.run` then `awaitIfClosed`). A UI fiber that cannot reach an interrupt point (a blocking call inside `Sync.defer`, `Thread.sleep`) keeps the terminal in raw mode for that long after `q`. On an INTERRUPT of the run the scope drain is detached (Kyo Scope.scala:346-360 'Open: no backpressure'), so there the restore does not wait. The Scaladoc only says 'The terminal is restored before this computation completes'.
findings.evidence: Tui.scala:134-142: `Sync.acquireReleaseWith(Session.open(...))(close) { ... Scope.run(runner.scoped(ui(runner.quit).map(runner.run))).andThen(inputFailed(session)) }`. Kyo 1.0.0-RC7 Fiber.scala:142-150 and Scope.scala:123-178 (sources in the scratchpad `kyosrc/core2/kyo`). The runner's own watchers avoid this by `Fiber.initUnscoped` + `unmountAll` (C2, R1 option b); the user's fibers do not. Same shape as the prototype and as `Headless.start`, so it is a known trade-off, not a regression.
findings.proposed_fix: No code change in T1. Add one sentence to the `Tui.run` Scaladoc (and AGENTS.md 'Rules for code'): 'After a quit, the run closes the UI's Scope (its `Fiber.init` fibers are interrupted and awaited) before it restores the terminal: a fiber that does not respond to the interrupt delays the restore.' If the user prefers the terminal first, the order can be changed in T2 by closing the session before the scope (the user's fibers would then print to the real stdout after the restore, which the capture no longer takes).

findings.claim: In the real load path the `NativeLoadFailed` message does not name the real cause: `NativeCrossterm.loadError` passes the wrapper (`ExceptionInInitializerError`, whose own message is null, or the second-try `NoClassDefFoundError`) as `error`, and the message is `s"... could not be loaded: $error"`, so a user reads 'could not be loaded: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError' and must dig into the stack trace for the `UnsatisfiedLinkError` text (the library name and platform). Also, the `Tui.run` Scaladoc lists `NotATerminal`, `NativeAccessDenied` and `TerminalIO` but not `NativeLoadFailed`.
findings.evidence: Crossterm.scala:310-316: `case NonFatal(_) | _: LinkageError => TuiError.NativeLoadFailed(e)` with `e` the wrapper; `causes(e)` (lines 320-325) already walks the chain but is used only for the `IllegalCallerException` test. NativeLoadErrorTest leaf 1 asserts `out.getCause eq in` and that the message has no `--enable-native-access`, so it does not pin the message text. Tui.scala:57-62 Scaladoc.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep `cause = e` (the full chain) but build the message from the root of `causes(e)` (the last element), for example `NativeLoadFailed(error: Throwable, root: Throwable)` or compute the root inside the case's message; add a NativeLoadErrorTest assertion that the message of `loadError(ExceptionInInitializerError(link))` contains 'libnative-x86_64-linux-crossterm.so cannot be found'. Add `NativeLoadFailed` to the `Tui.run` Scaladoc.

findings.claim: The input thread catches only `NonFatal(e)`: an `Error` that is not a `VirtualMachineError` (a `LinkageError` from a JNI call after the load, an `AssertionError`) ends the thread through the uncaught-exception handler, no `failure` is kept and no `Msg.Quit` is posted. The run then keeps drawing but never gets another key: `q` and Ctrl-C are dead (they are keys, read by this thread), and the run can end only from outside (`kill`, which does restore the terminal through Kyo's signal handling or the hook). The class Scaladoc says 'When the input fails, the thread keeps the failure and asks the run to end'.
findings.evidence: Session.scala:244-251: `catch case _: InterruptedException => () ; case NonFatal(e) => failure = e; discard(inbox.unsafe.putFiber(Msg.Quit))`. `NonFatal` excludes `LinkageError`, `VirtualMachineError`, `ThreadDeath`, `InterruptedException`, `ControlThrowable`. `NativeCrossterm.loadError` (Crossterm.scala:310-316) already treats `LinkageError` as a reportable failure; the input thread does not.
findings.proposed_fix: Catch `Throwable` after `InterruptedException`, let `VirtualMachineError` rethrow, and treat everything else as the failure (`failure = e; putFiber(Msg.Quit)`), so the run ends with `TuiError.TerminalIO(e)` and the terminal is restored. A SessionTest leaf with a port whose `poll` throws `UnsatisfiedLinkError` can pin it (the current leaf uses an `IOException`).

findings.claim: The Scaladoc of `RecordingControl.backend` says 'The runner's canvas resizes it on a resize', but `enter` returns the `Flushed` wrapper, and `Canvas.resize` resizes only a bare `TestBackend` (`backend match case tb: TestBackend => tb.resize(...)`), so a `Msg.Resize` through a `RecordingControl` never resizes its `TestBackend`: the canvas buffers change size, the backend does not, and a later `screen` read shows the old size. No current test resizes through `RecordingControl` (the kit uses a bare `TestBackend`), so nothing fails today.
findings.evidence: RecordingControl.scala:367-373 `RecordingControl.Flushed(backend, ...)` extends `Backend`, not `TestBackend`; Paint.scala:71-74 `case tb: TestBackend => tb.resize(s.w, s.h); case _ => ()`. SessionTest and TerminalIOTest never send a resize through a control.
findings.proposed_fix: Either fix the Scaladoc ('a resize does not reach this backend') or give `Flushed` a `resize` path (make `Canvas.resize` look through a small `Resizable` trait that both `TestBackend` wrappers implement). Test-source only.

findings.claim: The `terminal` job runs `sudo apt-get install -y expect` without `sudo apt-get update`. On `ubuntu-latest` the baked package index is often older than the mirror, and `apt-get install` then fails with a 404 on the `.deb` (a known intermittent failure of runner images), which would make the real-terminal job red for a reason unrelated to tui4s. The acceptance of 6.5 is 'the CI terminal job green 3 times before review'.
findings.evidence: ci.yml:61 `- run: sudo apt-get install -y expect`; no `apt-get update` step in the job. The PR 5 job had the same line (carried).
findings.proposed_fix: `- run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends expect`.

RELEASE ORDER (Session.close:87-104, TerminalIO.leave:132-167): canvas.close (under the backend monitor: waits for a draw in progress) -> input thread requestStop -> inbox close (fails pending puts/takes with Closed: verified in Kyo Channel.scala flush, the queueClosed branch) -> bounded join (2*poll+50 ms) -> leaveCommands (DisableBracketedPaste iff paste, Show, LeaveAlternateScreen) -> disableRawMode -> flush -> capture.stop -> sink.finish (ring printed to the real stderr) -> hook removed (not from inside the hook) -> R3 warning once -> first release error printed -> restored(). IDEMPOTENT, ONCE: Session.close is `synchronized` + `closed.compareAndSet`; the run's own release (Sync.acquireReleaseWith, Kyo's kernel Bracket with the exactly-once guarantee, release run synchronously) and the shutdown hook both call the same close(); the second caller waits on the monitor and no-ops. QUIT / INTERRUPT / FAILED UI / HANDLER PANIC: quit value and Tui.quit -> quitRequested flag + inbox.offer(Quit) -> Loop.done -> Sync.ensure(stop) -> Scope.run close -> inputFailed -> release. Interrupt -> the ensure/bracket release runs on the run fiber (TuiRunTest 'an interrupted run leaves the terminal', OS-34: the test polls `done`, never joins). A UI construction that throws -> Panic through the bracket -> release -> re-raised as it is after the restore (TerminalIOTest and TuiRunTest leaves). A handler that panics is caught by Dispatch.safe (Abort.run[Throwable], Result.Panic case) and logged through TuiLog, the run goes on. A TuiError thrown by Canvas.terminalIO (a failed write) is a Panic that Tui.runWith turns into the Abort failure (TuiRunTest 'a write to the terminal fails').

SIGTERM / SIGINT with a KyoApp main: Kyo's KyoAppInterrupts installs INT/TERM handlers, `raceFirst` interrupts the run fiber -> bracket release restores -> exit 130/143; the tui4s-restore hook on System.exit then waits on the Session monitor and no-ops. A plain main without Kyo handlers: the JVM runs the hook -> close() -> restore. No deadlock: the hook holds only the Session monitor and waits only for the backend monitor (held by a draw that waits for nothing) and the bounded thread join; the runner never takes the Session monitor; the hook never joins the run fiber.

INPUT THREAD (InputThread:206-256): a platform daemon thread; poll(pollMillis) then read, at most 512 queued events per batch with poll(0) between; it only maps (EventMapping, pure) and posts (putBatchFiber + CountDownLatch) — no drawing, no handler; stops on requestStop after the current poll; a full inbox makes it wait (backpressure), the close of the inbox releases the wait (Kyo Channel flush drains puts with Closed when the queue is closed; a batch larger than the capacity is offered item by item and the rest parked in priorityPuts, so inboxCapacity = 1 cannot deadlock). The null JNI read is dropped. A failing poll keeps the failure and posts Msg.Quit with a waiting put (SessionTest 'an input failure is kept and ends the run, also when the inbox is full'); Tui.inputFailed turns it into TuiError.TerminalIO after the restore (TuiRunTest).

The bundled native library is crossterm 0.29.0: `strings libnative-x86_64-linux-crossterm.so` from crossterm-0.31.0.jar gives `crossterm-0.29.0`, and the library links `core::unicode::unicode_data::uppercase::lookup`, which is consistent with `char_code_to_event` (an upper-case char gets SHIFT). The jatatui Java sources (tui/crossterm/*.java) pass the modifier bits through unchanged. EventMapping.scala:98-109 keeps `mods(ke.modifiers)`, and EventMappingTest:72 and :116-135 assert `Char('A')` with shift. Headless.keyOf (Headless.scala:330-337) builds `KeyboardEvent(k, Modifiers.none, Absent)`, and `paste` with `paste = false` (Headless.scala:186-198) claims to send the text 'as a terminal sends it'. Nothing records the gap: the PR body, AGENTS.md and examples/README.md say nothing about shift and the kit. A browser also sends shiftKey=true with 'A', so the kit is the outlier. Three limits on the claim. (2) 'No terminal sends' it is too strong. jatatui also ships the Windows library (`native-x86_64-windows-crossterm.dll` is in the jar), and on Windows crossterm takes shift from the key state, so Caps Lock gives `Char('A')` with no modifiers. The code expects Windows: Crossterm.stdinIsTerminal says 'True when it cannot be known (Windows)'. A browser with Caps Lock does the same. (3) Scope: the kit is C3 code, and plan 6.5 puts the Keymap.scala:159 lesson only in EventMappingTest, so a line under P-12 / known limits is enough for T1 if the kit change is deferred. The order is as described and is design-inherited, so the proposed Scaladoc sentence is the whole fix. Tui.scala:134-142: `Scope.run(runner.scoped(ui(runner.quit).map(runner.run)))` sits inside the `Sync.acquireReleaseWith` use; the restore is the release at line 135 (`opened.foreach(_.close())`). Kyo 1.0.0-RC7 (scratchpad kyosrc/core2/kyo) Fiber.scala:142-150: the release of `Fiber.init` is `fiber.interrupt.andThen(Async.useResult(promise)(result => own.close(result.error).andThen(own.await)))`, so it awaits the fiber's result; Scope.scala `run` ends with `finalizer.awaitIfClosed`, so a normal quit waits for every UI fiber before the bracket release restores the terminal; on an interrupt the drain is a detached spawn (Scope.scala:346-360 'Open: no backpressure'). The same order as the prototype (.work/proto/kyoui-runner/src/tui4s/kyoui/Tui.scala:76-90: `Sync.ensure(restore)` around `Scope.run`) and as the kit (Headless.scala:321 `Fiber.init` of the run inside the test's Scope). The runner's own fibers avoid the wait (`Fiber.initUnscoped` + `unmountAll`, Runner.scala:126-134); the user's `Fiber.init` fibers do not. No code change; a Scaladoc (and AGENTS.md) sentence.

Narrowed. (b) is right: Tui.scala:57-62 lists NotATerminal, NativeAccessDenied and TerminalIO but not NativeLoadFailed (AGENTS.md:134-135 does name it). (a) is right only for two cases; its premise is wrong for the main one. A JDK 25 probe (scratchpad probe/Probe.java) shows the JLS 12.4.2 rule: an Error thrown by a static initializer is thrown AS IS, so the first `new CrosstermJni()` gives the `UnsatisfiedLinkError` itself, and the NativeLoadFailed message then reads 'could not be loaded: java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: Native library libnative-x86_64-linux-crossterm.so cannot be found' (the root is named). javap of jatatui 0.31.0 crossterm-0.31.0.jar: `CrosstermJni.<clinit>` calls `NativeLoader.load`, catches only RuntimeException/Exception; `NativeLoader.loadPackaged` itself throws `UnsatisfiedLinkError` for a missing resource and `System.load` throws it for a bad library. The message does NOT name the root in two cases: an unknown platform (`NativeLoader.getPlatform` throws a RuntimeException, which the JVM wraps: the probe gives toString 'java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError', getMessage null), and a second `Tui.run` in the same JVM after a failed load (`NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class ...`, cause chain with the first error's text). So: add NativeLoadFailed to the Tui.run Scaladoc; optionally build the message from the root of `causes(e)`. The reviewer's proposed test input `ExceptionInInitializerError(link)` is a shape the JVM never produces; use `ExceptionInInitializerError(RuntimeException("Platform detection ..."))` and NativeLoadErrorTest's `secondTry` instead.

Session.scala:244-251 catches `InterruptedException` and `NonFatal(e)` only; Scala's NonFatal excludes VirtualMachineError, ThreadDeath, InterruptedException, LinkageError and ControlThrowable. A JNI native method binds at its first call, so a missing symbol surfaces as an UnsatisfiedLinkError in the input thread's first `poll`, not at load (Crossterm.scala:108-114 `loadError` treats a LinkageError at load, the thread does not). Consequence as stated: the daemon thread ends through the uncaught-exception handler (its stack trace goes to the captured System.err, so nothing shows on screen), `failure` stays null, no Msg.Quit is posted, and q and Ctrl-C are dead keys (Session.close only runs at the end of the run or from the shutdown hook). Mitigating facts: the same `catch NonFatal` is in the carried PR 5 code (666a8e3 Session.scala:238-243), and with the shipped jatatui jar every native symbol exists, so the trigger needs a broken library or an AssertionError in Java code. Fix as proposed (catch Throwable after InterruptedException, rethrow VirtualMachineError), with a SessionTest leaf whose port throws UnsatisfiedLinkError.

RecordingControl.scala:29-32 says 'The runner's canvas resizes it on a resize', but `enter` (lines 46-51) returns `RecordingControl.Flushed`, which extends `Backend`, not `TestBackend` (lines 63-64), and Canvas.resize (Paint.scala:69-79) resizes only `case tb: TestBackend`, so a Msg.Resize through a RecordingControl resizes the canvas buffers and leaves the TestBackend at its old size. The claim says that a Value(6) left in the inbox at quit time is the operative risk. The initial frame does not depend on the 300 ms. The app starts the set(6) fiber while the UI is being built, before `runner.run` mounts it (Tui.scala:140, `ui(runner.quit).map(runner.run)`). Runner.run then does `settleAndVerify(w0, input = false)` before the Initial frame (Runner.scala:147). The default settle is Quiescent(100 ms, confirm 2) (TuiOptions.scala:64). It waits until SchedulerProbe sees no queued or running task besides the runner, so a set(6) task that is queued holds the settle. The verify pass then re-reads `current` of the regions mounted in this step, so the Initial frame shows 'Count: 6' whatever the wall-clock time. The 300 ms only matters in a double corner: the 100 ms settle bound expires while the set(6) task still has not run, AND the runner then misses a message for 300 ms after the set. The 300 ms timer starts only after set(6). The suites run one at a time in the forked JVM (modules/core/build.sbt:66), and the leaf took 332 to 338 ms in all 8 logs (t1-check.log:357 and the others). Waiting with `eventually` before the quit is a harmless extra hardening, but the leaf is not a real flake source.
